findings.complexity: Pure functional helper O(n) time/O(n) output; actual native method O(n) time/O(1) auxiliary storage (count scan plus backward scan, scalar cursors only), n<=10,000.
findings.effects: Pure solve returns a fresh vector and never mutates input. Native methods write the original fixed-length buffer, do not resize or allocate an input-sized helper, and implicitly return PythonNone/JSundefined. JS class delegates to the same standalone duplicateZeros function exported under the official name. Native permission is a distinct mutable-input effect contract, not read-only compatibility.
interfaces: JS duplicateZeros(arr) named export and Solution.duplicateZeros(arr); all three native entries have separate execution observations
findings.numeric: All digits0..9, zero counts<=10,000 and virtual indices<=19,999; exact bounded arithmetic.
findings.semantics: Pure solve appends each digit and an extra zero when needed, stopping at original length. Native invariant: before processing indexr backward, zeros counts zeros in original0..r and unprocessed elements remain intact. The virtual destinationr+zeros lies at or right ofr; saving value before writes and decrementing zeros for a zero preserves earlier unread cells. Only destinations in0..size-1 are written, correctly truncating duplicate zeros at the right boundary. Tailzero, singletonzero, allzero and allnonzero inputs follow the same invariant.

findings.complexity: Two scans over exactly256 bins, O(256) time/O(1) auxiliary storage excluding output.
findings.effects: The count vector is read only; the five-element output is a fresh list/array of numbers.
interfaces: Python Solution.sampleStats(count); JS sampleStats and Solution.sampleStats delegate; wrapper execution not claimed
findings.numeric: Total<=10^9 and weighted numerator<=255*10^9=255,000,000,000, below2^53; integral JS intermediates exact. Floating means lie in[0,255], with ordinary division error far below public absolute1e-5 tolerance; medians are exact integer/half-integer values. Existing predicate checks ordered five-tuple, finite numeric entries and abs(error)<=1e-5; bools excluded.
findings.semantics: Returns exactly [minimum,maximum,mean,median,mode]. Nonzero bins identify endpoints; the unique largest count determines mode. Weighted median ranks are floor((total+1)/2) and floor(total/2)+1: same rank for odd sizes, neighboring ranks for even sizes. First cumulative crossings are recorded once and averaged.
